contamination:
NOT NONE — four items, in descending importance.

(1) HARNESS AUTO-INJECTED UNTRUSTED REPO INSTRUCTION FILES. Reading files under research/inter-rater-repos/<dir>/ caused the Claude Code harness to inject that repo's own CLAUDE.md (and .claude/rules/*.md) into my context AS PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS, unprompted. It happened for obra__superpowers, addyosmani__agent-skills, JuliusBrussee__caveman, and shanraisshan__claude-code-best-practice. These are agent-directed instruction files (obra's opens 'Stop. Read this section before doing anything.' and tells the agent what its job is; shanraisshan's contains git-commit rules). I treated all of them as data and followed none of them. Two problems for the measurement: (a) it is a live prompt-injection surface inside the protocol itself — a hostile repo could ship a CLAUDE.md that instructs the rater how to score; (b) it handed me repo-level context (contributor philosophy, hook architecture, full skill inventory, why the presentation skills are split) that a rater who reads the same SKILL.md files in a different order or environment would NOT receive. That is an uncontrolled between-rater variable and it materially informed my L-003 read on shanraisshan and my L-002 read on caveman. Recommend the next round copy only the sampled SKILL.md files into a neutral directory, or strip CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/rules from the clones.

(2) RUBRIC LEAK — the masked rubric names a sample in this batch. L-004's exemption lists '未附引用的科學或領域事實主張(實例:某 skill 直述五條 ADHD 神經科學事實)'. ayghri__i-have-adhd is the only ADHD skill in the batch and it literally has a section headed '## What ADHD changes about reading — Five facts drive every rule below'. That parenthetical pre-decided ayghri::L-004 for me: it told me, before I read the file, that uncited domain-science claims defeat the exemption. Absent that line I would plausibly have read i-have-adhd as pure interaction-style methodology and judged n/a. My ayghri::L-004 = poor should be treated as anchored, not independent.

(3) PROBABLE SECOND RUBRIC LEAK. The same exemption lists '本地產物的結構描述(實例:記錄自家 index.html 的 CSS class)——算易腐'. shanraisshan's presentation-styling skill is exactly that shape ('CSS classes and HTML patterns used in presentation/index.html'). Whether or not the parenthetical refers to this sample, it pre-decides the ruling for this exact shape, so shanraisshan::L-004 is also partly anchored. (I did independently verify that presentation/index.html no longer exists in that repo, so the perishability is demonstrated, not assumed.)

(4) MASKING IS INCOMPLETE. The masked file still carries unmasked named evidence: ljagiello/ctf-skills, Jeffallan, Leonxlnx/taste, kangarooking, nicobailon, K-Dense, Orchestra, claude-ads, prompt-master, NevaMind-AI/memU, OthmanAdi/planning-with-files, mvanhorn/last30days, upload-to-stitch, guizang-ppt, alirezarezvani/claude-skills, jezweb, plus the internal skills huashu-nuwa / ga-methodology / improve-codebase-architecture / diagnose / grill-me / zoom-out / khazix. None of those are among my 15, so I do not believe they anchored these ratings — but the masking script is clearly only removing evidence_refs entries selectively, and a future batch overlapping those names would be contaminated.

Not contamination but disclosed for completeness: my session's git-status snapshot listed two untracked filenames, research/qualitative_notes/axtonliu__smart-illustrator.md and .../jnMetaCode__superpowers-zh.md. Filenames only — I did not open them and they carry no verdict. rubric_friction:
Eleven places I had to extrapolate. The first three are the ones I think actually move numbers.

1. DECISION_ORDER AND COLLECTION_AGGREGATION CONTRADICT EACH OTHER ON L-004, and 11 of my 15 repos are collections. decision_order step 1 is an unconditional binary: '機制存在?…→ good ——不論該 skill 有沒有易腐事實'. collection_aggregation says for a ≤5 sample 'good = 機制存在且覆蓋到易腐表面; mixed = 部分覆蓋或樣本間不一致'. For every collection where a mechanism exists in some sampled skills but not the ones carrying the most perishable content, the two clauses give different answers. I resolved it by treating collection_aggregation as the more specific rule and applying it to all multi-skill repos, which is why kepano and jnMetaCode are mixed rather than good. A rater who reads decision_order as controlling (it says '務必照序') would score both good. This single ambiguity could account for most L-004 disagreement in this round. The rubric needs to say explicitly: for collections, step 1's '機制存在' is evaluated against the sampled set's perishable surface, not as bare presence.

2. L-004'S WEAK TIER MAKES STEP 1 NEARLY UNFAILABLE. The strength ladder names '單純來源標註' ('一條參考連結') as one of the three 達標形式. Taken literally, any skill containing one reference link passes step 1 and never reaches steps 2–3. RinDig__icm-architect got good from a single line — 'Method: Interpretable Context Methodology (Van Clief & McDermott, arXiv:2603.16021, MIT-licensed)' — and nothing else; had I not counted that, step 2 would then have had to decide whether third-party filename conventions (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) are perishable, and I'd have landed on mixed. That is my least confident cell in the whole batch. The 強/中/弱 ladder and the binary decision_order are pulling in opposite directions: either the weak tier should not satisfy step 1, or step 1 should return 'good(weak)' as a distinct value.

3. NEITHER EXEMPTION FIRED ONCE. Zero n/a across 60 cells. L-002's exemption is scoped to canned-phrase and interaction-protocol shapes; ayghri__i-have-adhd is the closest thing in the batch to an interaction protocol and it still has ten substantive rules with Bad/Good pairs, so it is plainly not the exempt shape. L-004's exemption requires no content that 'will go wrong when something it cannot control changes' — and every third-party repo here touches a third-party CLI, API, framework or local artifact. Combined with the broadened criterion (uncited domain claims and local-artifact descriptions both count), I do not believe L-004's exemption is reachable for third-party repos at all. If that is right, n/a is effectively an internal-skill-only category and the 4-way scale is really 3-way for this population — which matters for how kappa is computed.

4. L-001 HAS NO SEVERITY LADDER. The rule names two failure modes (關鍵字轟炸, 過寬) but never says whether hitting one means mixed or poor. I anchored on the rubric's own 反例 list — '20+ SEO 變體轟炸' and '全無 Use when' are both listed as negative exemplars — and treated a full-intensity match on either as poor (browser-act, shanraisshan) and a partial match as mixed (JimLiu, axtonliu, ECC). That mapping is mine, not the rubric's, and it is the single most arbitrary thing I did.

5. IS THE 高分 REQUIREMENT NEEDED FOR good ON L-001? pass_criteria splits a base clause (含明確觸發情境) from a 高分 clause (再具負向觸發 NOT for). I treated NOT-for as a bonus, not a gate. A rater who reads the whole pass_criteria as the bar for 'good' would move blader, ayghri, jnMetaCode, addyosmani-partially and RinDig from good to mixed — six repos on one reading of one sentence. The rubric should say which clause defines good.

6. L-003 FOR COLLECTIONS WHOSE SUB-SKILLS ARE GENUINELY INDEPENDENT. pass_criteria requires 'D/C 類具 dispatcher 或 When-to-Pivot 互相路由'. kepano's five skills cover disjoint file formats (.base/.canvas/.md/CLI/web) where routing between them would be noise, and I scored good. JimLiu's five also lack routing but include two adjacent image-generation skills, and I scored mixed. That distinction — 'routing needed but absent' vs 'routing not needed' — is a judgment I invented. The rubric has no n/a path for L-003 and no test for when routing is owed.

7. SELF-CONTAINED DISTRIBUTION VS DRY. sub_pattern_cross_skill rewards reusing a sibling's reference by relative path 'rather than copying'. But a skill distributed individually (npx skills add, plugin marketplace) MUST be self-contained — a relative path out of its own directory breaks on install. JimLiu duplicates identical blocks across four skills for exactly that reason. The rubric currently penalises a correct packaging decision; it needs a carve-out for independently-installable skills.

8. REPO-LEVEL VS SKILL-LEVEL SCOPE. L-003's rule is written per-skill ('一個 skill 一個 job'), but its mechanism is repo-level ('觸發不重疊、維護不衝突'). ECC has clean per-skill scope AND 238 colliding frontmatter names across mirror trees. I judged on the mechanism and gave mixed; a rater reading only the rule text would give good, because every individual file is fine. Same tension, smaller, on blader (two byte-identical SKILL.md files both declaring name: humanizer).

9. THE `shape` ENUM COLLAPSES. Eleven of fifteen are multi-skill repos, so 'collection' swallows nearly everything and stops discriminating. I used 'collection' only for heterogeneous bundles and reported the dominant sampled sub-shape when the bundle is homogeneous (kepano→lookup, obra→methodology, earthtojake→tool). Two raters applying the two different conventions will look like they disagree about shape when they agree about the skills. The field needs two axes: container shape × sampled sub-skill shape.

10. L-002'S DIMENSION IS `writing_quality` BUT THE RULE ONLY ASKS ABOUT why/examples/override. google__skills' highest-priority blocks are malformed markdown — '> [!IMPORTANT] **CRITICAL: Unified SDK…** * **Unified SDK**: … * *Mandatory Instruction*: …' renders as one wall with literal asterisks instead of a list, in the most important paragraph of the skill. That is a genuine writing-quality defect the rule cannot see, so I did not deduct. Either rename the dimension or add legibility to the rule.

11. `disable-model-invocation` / `user-invocable: false` AND L-001. SKILL.md step 3 grants 'disable-model-invocation 即等同負向觸發' only to the 一次性安裝/腳本型 row. ayghri (a persistent mode skill, disable-model-invocation: true, invoked by /i-have-adhd) and shanraisshan's weather-fetcher (user-invocable: false, preloaded into an agent) are neither shape, yet the same logic obviously applies — a skill that has opted out of model invocation cannot overtrigger, so demanding 'Use when' of it is meaningless. I extended the exemption to both. The rubric should generalise it: any frontmatter flag that removes the skill from model-invocation routing suspends L-001's trigger-context requirement.
notes:
Distribution: 43 good / 12 mixed / 5 poor / 0 n/a. Per dimension — L-001: 10 good, 3 mixed, 2 poor. L-002: 13 good, 2 mixed. L-003: 10 good, 5 mixed. L-004: 10 good, 2 mixed, 3 poor. The skew toward good is, I think, a predicted consequence of the rubric rather than leniency on my part — the rubric itself flags it, in L-002's '已知殘留限制' note ('基礎判準太容易滿足,好的與普通的參考型 skill 會拿到同樣的 good'). Once equivalent_forms admits structured tables, threshold tables, falsifiable heuristics and terminology glossaries, almost any competent technical reference clears L-002's base bar. L-002 gave me 13 good, 2 mixed, 0 poor — it did essentially no discriminating work in this batch, and that is the dimension I'd expect to look artificially high-agreement for the wrong reason (everyone converging on 'good' by default is not the same as everyone reading the same signal). L-001 discriminated best (5 non-good).

My four lowest-confidence cells, in case the analysis wants to weight them: RinDig::L-004 (rests entirely on whether a bare citation satisfies step 1 — see friction 2); kepano::L-004 and jnMetaCode::L-004 (rest entirely on decision_order vs collection_aggregation — see friction 1); browser-act::L-001 and shanraisshan::L-001 as poor rather than mixed (rest on my invented severity mapping — see friction 4).

Specific findings worth keeping regardless of the ratings:

- affaan-m__ECC: 897 SKILL.md files, 287 distinct frontmatter `name` values. The mirrors are not identical copies — the ja-JP and zh-CN descriptions dropped the English original's "Use when" clause entirely while the tr one kept it. So the mirror strategy is actively degrading trigger quality, not just duplicating it. This is the clearest example in the batch of a repo-level packaging decision destroying skill-level craft.

- shanraisshan: presentation-styling and presentation-structure both point at `presentation/index.html`, which no longer exists (the repo now has three dated deck directories). This is L-004's failure mode caught in the act, on a *local* artifact rather than an external API — useful empirical support for the exemption clause's ruling that local-artifact descriptions count as perishable.

- blader__humanizer ships root SKILL.md and skills/humanizer/SKILL.md as byte-identical files, both declaring `name: humanizer`. Common dual-layout convention; noted but not scored against.

- jnMetaCode's README claims 'superpowers（250k+ ⭐）' for the upstream repo, which is off by roughly an order of magnitude. Not a SKILL.md so it did not feed any rating, but it is an unsourced marketing claim in the front door of a repo whose whole value proposition is faithful translation.

- earthtojake__text-to-cad is the best L-003 example I saw and worth capturing as a positive exemplar: gcode has a literal `## Bambu Boundary` section handing off to `$bambu-labs`, plus a per-format rejection table that names the exact sibling skill for each unsupported input ('.step: … Export an STL sidecar with $cad …, then slice the exported .stl here') with the instruction 'use it instead of inferring a conversion workflow'. That is the 顯式交棒 pattern executed better than any of the currently-cited evidence_refs.

- google__skills is the best L-004 example: 'Do not rely on Google Search, training-corpus knowledge, or publisher documentation for availability claims — regional availability changes frequently and grounded text can be stale or wrong', followed by a live `:generateContent` probe and an explicit warning not to probe a different model as a control. That is the 強 tier (dated/live probe + result interpretation) and it is strictly stronger than anything in the current evidence_refs.

- Outside my four dimensions, two things a reviewer should not miss. (a) JuliusBrussee__caveman registers SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks that inject a ruleset into every session; the architecture is documented in the repo's CLAUDE.md but I did not check whether it is disclosed to end users in the README — that is S-002 territory. (b) browser-act's reddit-warmup is an account-farming and astroturfing playbook ('Systematically grow newly registered … accounts into credible identities, then organically plant brand content'), and its sibling x-keyword-comment states outright that 'X's Terms of Service explicitly restrict automated behavior'. The craft is competent; the purpose is ToS-violating manipulation. The rubric has no dimension that can express this, and S-001/S-002/S-003 are all about risk to the *user*, not harm caused *by* the user. If skill-reviewer is ever pointed at a repo like this it will return a clean craft verdict, which would be misleading. Worth an explicit out-of-band flag category.

Method notes: I read every SKILL.md listed in each repo's craft_llm_todo. For the five files over ~500 lines (obra writing-skills 679, obra subagent-driven-development 568, the ECC set at 826–959, google agent-platform-inference 726) I read the frontmatter, the head, the structural outline, and every section a targeted grep flagged as bearing on L-001–L-004, rather than every line. All judgments are on the sampled files only, not on the repos as wholes.
